papers.title: Small-Scale Experiments: Are We There Yet?
papers.summary: Sample: introduces a method that improves efficiency without loss of quality. The approach is validated against strong baselines on standard benchmarks.
papers.abstract: Sample abstract: Small-scale experiments remain the dominant evaluation protocol in much of the literature, yet their predictive value for production-scale systems is rarely quantified. We study the correlation between small- and large-scale outcomes across a suite of training runs, identify the regimes in which the ordering of methods is preserved, and characterize where it breaks down. Our results suggest concrete guidelines for when a small-scale result should be trusted.

papers.title: DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference
papers.summary: Sample: proposes a lightweight technique addressing a key bottleneck. Experiments show consistent gains across several settings.
papers.abstract: Sample abstract: KV-cache memory dominates the footprint of long-context LLM inference. We propose an eviction policy that scores cached entries by their KL contribution to the output distribution rather than by attention mass alone, yielding a criterion that is cheap to compute and stable across layers. On long-context benchmarks the method retains quality at substantially reduced cache budgets.

papers.title: Derivative Computation in PINNs: Automatic Differentiation, Finite Differences and Beyond
papers.abstract: Sample abstract: Physics-informed neural networks require derivatives of the network output with respect to its inputs. We compare automatic differentiation against finite-difference and spectral alternatives in terms of cost, accuracy, and conditioning, and show that the best choice depends on the stiffness of the underlying operator rather than on the architecture.
